To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

glycogen content in livers of rats on a controlled‐feeding schedule was determined by chemical analysis, and correlated with the cytochemistry of hepatic glycogens and the fine structure of hepatocyte glycogen particles.
the fine structure of glycogen particles is dependent upon the glycogen content of hepatocytes and that the glycogen content is dependent upon the fasting state of rats.
glycogen content of liver cells from fasted rats correlates with the amount of glycogen seen with PA/S and the number of glycogenic particles in electron micrographs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the glycogen‐containing particles of the liver cell.
the study of hepatic glycogenesis and glycogenolysis in rats maintained on a controlled schedule of feeding.
the relationship of glycogen metabolism and fine structure of liver tissue from rats on a feeding schedule and from fasted and refed animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glycogen depletion in hepatocytes occurs by a process of dissolution of the α and β particles.
the glycogen particles are the structural units of glycogen and that the chemical determination of hepatic glycogenesis is an accurate measure of the amount of glycogen present in the liver.
glycogen is stored in the form of α and β particles which are located throughout the cytoplasm of liver cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glycogen is stored in large masses in hepatocytes of fasted rats.
chemical, cytochemical, and ultrastructural studies of hepatic glycogenesis in the rat are correlated with the fasting state of an animal.
the glycogen particles of the rat liver cell have a high degree of structural organization, and this organization is related to the metabolic state of the liver cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correlation between the chemical determination of hepatic glycogenesis, cytochemical determination of glycogen, and fine structure of liver cell is very good.
glycogen depletion occurs in the liver of the rat in a predictable manner.
glycogen is a dynamic molecule that can be rapidly mobilized and stored.
